page.overview:
Who is Dr. Alan Grant?

Dr. Alan Grant is one of the two main protagonists (Alongside Rexy) of the Jurassic Park franchise, serving as the primary protagonist of Jurassic Park and Jurassic Park III, one of the three unseen overarching protagonists of Jurassic World, and one of the six main protagonists (Ellie Sattler, Ian Malcolm, Claire Dearing, Owen Grady, and Kayla Watts) of Jurassic World: Dominion. He is a paleontologist who was invited by John Hammond to his dinosaur park, Jurassic Park. Grant is portrayed very differently over the various canons.

Alan Grant was born in the United States on a currently unknown date, although the Jurassic Park script states that he was in his mid-thirties in 1993, which would place his year of birth at approximately 1958. He became interested in dinosaurs at a very young age, with Triceratops, one of the best-known ceratopsids in North America, being his favorite species during his childhood; A wide variety of new fossil species were discovered and cataloged in the 1960s, during Grant's childhood, and the following decade led to even more finds in areas of Africa and South America.

Grant attended a currently unknown institution (possibly Montana State University, Bozeman) where he received a higher education in the paleontological field; If you attended EMU in the late 1980s, in your early twenties, you would probably have studied alongside the famous paleontologist Jack Horner, with whom you share many views (including a strong sense of rivalry with paleontologist Robert Bakker). and whom he seems to respect as an authority in his field. He obtained a doctorate in the 1990s and specialized in the paleobiology of deinonychosaurids, based specifically on the classification system proposed by Gregory S. Paul in his book Predatory Dinosaurs of the World, in which many deinonychosaurid dromaeosaurids are grouped into the genus Velociraptor.

He worked collaboratively with other paleontologists over the course of his career, including paleobotanist Ellie Sattler, with whom he became romantically involved in the early 1990s; Dr. Sattler was interested in eventually having children, while Grant had no interest in starting a family and did not get along well with children. At one point they adopted a blue and yellow macaw named Jack, whom they raised together and taught him to talk.

Also known as: Grant, Dr. Grant.
